newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights -- USDA.

text.p: USDA cotton export sales highlights in latest reporting week:

Net Upland sales of 1,400 running bales (RB)--the second lowest of the marketing year--were mainly the result of increases for Mexico (5,200 RB), China (4,700 RB), and Japan (1,200 RB) being partially offset by net changes in marketing year of 9,000 RB for Canada.
Sales of 65,700 RB for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year were primarily for Mexico (25,500 RB), Canada (9,000 RB), Thailand (8,000 RB), and China (7,500 RB).

Exports of 109,500 RB were 28 percent below the previous week and 12 percent less than the 4-week average. Western Hemisphere destinations accounted for 47 percent of the week's shipments; Asian, 35 percent; West European, 17 percent; and African, 1 percent. The major recipients were Mexico (19,500 RB), Brazil (18,500 RB), Turkey (15,300 RB), China (13,000 RB), and Indonesia (10,400 RB).
